newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabian stocks rise 12 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabian stocks rise 12 percent in 1996.

text.p: Saudi Arabian stock market ended 1996 some 12 percent higher, with market capitalisation reaching almost 172 billion riyals ($45.9 billion) from 153 billion at end-1995, the Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency (SAMA) said on Thursday.
"The Saudi stock market witnessed a good recovery during 1996," SAMA said in a report, adding that the all-share index closed the year at 153.1 points, compared to 136.76 at end-1995.
The total value of shares traded rose over nine percent to 25.4 billion riyals versus a previous 23.2 billion.
The number of shares traded was up over 18 percent to 137.8 million from 116.6 million for 1995, but the number of transactions ebbed to 283,759 from 291,742 in 1995.
SAMA said the average daily value traded for 1996 was 85 million riyals, an increase of over nine percent on the 77.7 million riyals a day recorded in 1995.
The average daily turnover of shares reached 463,000 compared to 390,000 in 1995.
At 10.4 billion riyals, or 41 percent, banking was the most active sector in terms of value traded.
Services stocks were the most active in terms of turnover with 48 million shares changing hands.
With shares worth 3.6 billion riyals traded in 30,500 deals, Riyad Bank was the most heavily traded stock in the year.
Some 3.4 billion riyals worth of Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) shares changed hands in 20,500 transactions.
SAMA said Saudi Cement shares worth 2.6 billion riyals were traded in 20,400 transactions.
Saudi Cement had the highest turnover in the year, with 15.6 million shares traded. Riyad Bank followed with 15.4 million.

SAMA said 3.85 million new shares worth 732.5 million riyals were issued in the year. Saudi Investment Bank issued 3.6 million of these -- half through a rights issue and half by public subscription. Zoujaj offered the rest in a rights issue. ($1=3.75 riyals)
